# Architecture

Snapshot of the **segv** cluster as observed on 2026-10-17, compared against this repo and the diagrams in `docs/hld/`.

Method: read-only `kubectl` (`infra/clusters/segv/kube.conf`) plus a read-only SSH session to `core@tachyon.lan` (key auth works). Nothing was changed on the cluster. Items marked *not verified* could not be confirmed from either source.

## Overview

| | |
|---|---|
| Cluster | `segv`, a single bare-metal node: `tachyon.lan` (10.0.0.6), controller-labelled and schedulable, so it also runs all workloads |
| Kubernetes | server v1.29.3, node kubelet v1.29.2, containerd 1.6.23 |
| OS | Fedora CoreOS 40 base (`40.20240416.3.1`), kernel 6.8.5, rebased with `rpm-ostree` onto `ghcr.io/alxbl/lab/fcos` (ZFS layer). Booted image is the 2024-05-20 build and the 2024-07-15 build is the other deployment |
| Hardware | 8-disk ZFS `raidz2` pool `data` (4.1T, ONLINE, no errors) mounted at `/var/data`. OS on `/dev/sda4` (xfs, 466G, 37% used) |
| Provisioning | Terraform wrapping a fork of Typhoon (`alxbl/typhoon`, ref `alxbl/aarch64`), matchbox and PXE |
| GitOps | ArgoCD v3.5.2, app-of-apps tracking `HEAD` of `github.com/alxbl/lab` |
| CNI | Calico v3.27.2 (installed by Typhoon, not by ArgoCD) |
| Service mesh | Istio 1.21.0 (Helm charts via ArgoCD), sidecar injection per namespace |

Both the node OS and Kubernetes are about two years behind. The `build-fcos-zfs` workflow builds weekly but the node has not rebased since July 2024.

## Provisioning

- `scripts/bootstrap.sh` starts matchbox and a proxyDHCP dnsmasq (`build/bootstrap/docker-compose.yml`, `dnsmasq.conf`) on the admin workstation, runs `terraform apply` in `infra/clusters/segv`, then tears the PXE stack down.
- `segv.tf` uses the Typhoon `bare-metal/fedora-coreos/kubernetes` module. Matchbox is `th1nk.lan:8080`, the node is identified by MAC, installs to `/dev/sda`, and gets the `wipe-root` butane snippet so the root FS is wiped on reprovision.
- The Typhoon module pins `os_version = 39.20240112.3.0`. The running node has since moved to FCOS 40 via rpm-ostree.
- After bootstrap the cluster is self-sufficient. ArgoCD and the catalogs are applied separately.

## Networking

| | |
|---|---|
| Node/LAN | 10.0.0.0/16 (node 10.0.0.6) |
| Pod CIDR | 10.2.0.0/16 (Calico IPPool `default-ipv4-ippool`) |
| Service CIDR | 10.3.0.0/16 |
| Ingress | Istio gateway `istio-ingress/https-in-gw`, TLS cert `https-in-gw-cert` from cert-manager ClusterIssuer `letsencrypt-issuer` |
| Routing | VirtualServices on that gateway: `home-assistant-vsvc`, `vaultwarden-vsvc`, `https-external` (`/photos` to photoprism), `tcp-virtualservice` (smbd) |
| Policy | Istio `AuthorizationPolicy` (ingress allow-lists, `deny-non-mtls` in `argocd`) and per-app Kubernetes `NetworkPolicy` objects. OLM namespace has a default-deny |

The pod CIDR overlaps the dev environment's `qemu0` bridge (10.2.0.0/24), which is why the dev cluster uses 10.22/16 and 10.33/16.

## Storage

- OpenEBS provides four classes: `zfs-rwo` (ZFS LocalPV CSI, `Retain`), `zfs-rwx` (NFS provisioner, which creates a backing `zfs-rwo` PVC in the `openebs` namespace), and the stock `openebs-hostpath` / `openebs-device`.
- All persistent data lives in datasets of the `data` pool, one per PVC (9 datasets, 11 PVCs including NFS backing volumes).
- Largest consumers: media NFS backing volume (1.7T used), smbd backing volume (247G), photoprism cache (23G).

## GitOps layout

```
infra/system/argocd      installs ArgoCD, the `root` app and `system-catalog` app
infra/k8s/catalog        meta-chart: Applications for general workloads   (root app)
infra/system/catalog     meta-chart: Applications for system components   (system-catalog app)
charts/                  own Helm charts
infra/k8s/*, infra/system/*   kustomize apps
```

Two AppProjects exist: `default` (most workloads) and `system` (`argocd`, `calico`, `cnpg`, `cnpg-operator`, `keycloak`, `olm`, `system-catalog`).

## Workloads by namespace

| Namespace | Contents |
|---|---|
| `argocd` | ArgoCD v3.5.2 (server, repo-server, application/applicationset controllers, dex, redis, notifications) |
| `cert-manager` | cert-manager, ClusterIssuer `letsencrypt-issuer` |
| `cnpg-system` | CloudNativePG operator (chart 0.29.0) |
| `home` | adguard, home-assistant (StatefulSet, upstream pajikos chart), vaultwarden |
| `istio-system`, `istio-ingress` | istiod, ingress gateway |
| `kube-system` | Calico, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, istio-cni, OpenEBS ZFS CSI, static control-plane pods |
| `media` | aquisition (sonarr, radarr, prowlarr, qbt, pmp-monitor), immich (server, machine-learning, valkey, CNPG cluster `immich-database`), jellyfin, photoprism (scaled to 0), smbd |
| `monitoring` | prometheus, grafana, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter (plain manifests) |
| `olm`, `operators` | Operator Lifecycle Manager, Keycloak operator v26.7.3 (no Keycloak instance exists yet) |
| `openebs` | OpenEBS operators, NFS provisioner and the two NFS backing pods |
| `satisfactory` | Deployment scaled to 0 |
| `system` | Velero v1.13.0 and its `node-agent` |

## Backups / DR

- Velero schedule `backup-pv-daily` (03:00 daily). The latest backup completed 13 hours before this snapshot, and the daily series is unbroken for at least the last 5 days.
- BackupStorageLocation `azure` is `Available`. It targets an Azure Blob storage account. Data movement uses the Velero `node-agent` (kopia), as in `docs/hld/backups.drawio`.
- The Velero pod has restarted 1881 times in 413 days (last restart 16 hours ago).
- The external-drive `rsync` copy mentioned in `README.md` was *not verified*.

## Dev cluster

See `DEVELOPMENT.md`. Note that dev uses Cilium, while segv uses Calico, so CNI-related behaviour does not carry over.
